questions.question: How many promoted public strategy traces can the C++ transition microkernel follow with 100% support and zero SIG mismatches?
questions.why_it_matters: This measures readiness for any future C++ rollout core.

questions.question: Is explicit random-outcome transport enough for all rare random effects, or should the C++ core eventually own its own RNG stream?
questions.why_it_matters: Jace ultimate proved transcript transport is clean for differential checking, but tournament-speed C++ may need a stronger RNG contract.

questions.question: Can a tiny action-ranker trained on readable public policies enter the population as a competitive public agent?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the lowest-risk neural/ML bridge before RL.

questions.question: Do action-ranker context features reveal only legal public observations and own hand, or did a hidden state sneak into the dataset?
questions.why_it_matters: Feature datasets can silently reintroduce the exact leakage the DecisionFrame boundary was designed to prevent.

questions.question: Does an imitation ranker beat the weak policies it imitates, or only average them into worse play?
questions.why_it_matters: Imitation can smooth away sharp conditional behavior.

questions.question: How often does Jace ultimate actually decide games in promoted populations versus merely appearing in coverage decks?
questions.why_it_matters: The C++ debt was technical; now we can ask whether the mechanic is strategically central.

questions.question: Is Python-to-C++ transport overhead now larger than the C++ transition work itself?
questions.why_it_matters: A full C++ core may only pay off after batching records or moving more state into C++.

questions.question: Does a policy trained/imitation-fitted on mixed 20/40 life frames learn life-aware action preferences or collapse to the majority pattern?
questions.why_it_matters: The life dial is a construction and play context; learned methods must not ignore it.
